name: Nose-lifting or slimming massage

lead: Nose massage is the practice of pressing, pinching or rubbing the nose, often daily, in the hope of making it narrower, higher-bridged or more lifted. It is described in beauty and appearance communities as a no-cost, non-surgical option.

Proponents say repeated pressure gradually reshapes the nose. Surgeons quoted about similar pressure methods say bone and cartilage are not changed by outside pressure, and no published studies testing the practice were located.

paras: Users press along the sides and bridge of the nose or pinch the tip for a few minutes, usually daily as part of a skincare or face routine. It needs no equipment.
No documented harms specific to the practice were located. General skin irritation from frequent rubbing is possible.

angle.text: Beauty communities describe daily nose rubbing or pinching as a free, non-surgical way to slim or lift the nose through gradual tissue reshaping. The claim rests on anecdote, and no studies have tested it.

lead: Nose-lifting or slimming massage refers to the practice of pressing, pinching or rubbing the nose, often daily, with the aim of making it narrower, higher-bridged or more lifted. It is described in beauty and appearance communities as a no-cost, non-surgical option.

paras: Proponents describe repeated manual pressure or stroking along the bridge and sides of the nose, sometimes combined with facial massage routines. The practice is related to nose taping and other pressure-based approaches that aim to change nasal shape without surgery.

The external nose is built from bone, cartilage and overlying soft tissue. Surgeons' position, as reported in coverage of related practices such as nose taping, is that permanent reshaping of the nose requires surgery and that non-surgical pressure methods cannot alter bone or cartilage.[1]
